metas.name: Lushly Forested and Mountainous Landscape -  West Arg
metas.note:
This landscape is mainly characterized by:

  • forested, high and rocky mountains
  • lush vegetation;
  • predominance of pine trees, spruce trees and larches; glacial lakes;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Azorella Prolifera - Cushion-looking plant
metas.note: Azorella Prolifera is a light green cushion-looking plant with tiny yellow flowers. This plant may be found throughout the Patagonia region. However, as it was said, the appearance (talking mainly about hue) of shrubs and other plants depends on the month/season. The season that provides such a look is late spring or early summer.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Cabo Blanco - Lighthouse
metas.note: Cabo Blanco can be recognized by this rock with a lighthouse.
metas.footer: Image from The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid, description by me

metas.name: Caviahue Copahue - Snow coverage + Mountains
metas.note: Snowy mountains with cloudy mountain tops and dark dirt road
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - April
metas.note:
The April autumn may be tricky and sometimes hard to recognize. April on the east coast looks like a mix of March and June, like… it kinda looks like winter coverage but it’s not really it.

April has additional two different appearances:

  • Comodoro Rivadavia hills in April coverage (may look like March);
  • mostly cloudy + visible mountain range in the distance to the north;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - December
metas.note: The December summer landscape in Chubut looks very distinctive mainly because of the characteristic light soil and green shrubland. That type of landscape is also mentioned in another meta called “Very Green Shrubland”.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - Jan,Feb,Mar
metas.note:
The January, February and March summer generally looks very sunny, dry with greenish shrubs.

These months look identical. However, March has additional three different appearances:

  • very dry-looking March;
  • Península Valdés landscape;
  • cloudy March;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - June
metas.note: The June winter almost everywhere looks the same or very similar. However, there is a small stretch of RP1 between Rawson and Puerto Madryn on which you can find a June sunrise coverage.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - October
metas.note:
The October spring may be quite hard to recognize at the first time but after some practicing, it will be recognizable easily. The green color of shrubland in October has such distinctive vibes. The shrubland is like a mix of shrubs that have vivid green color and weak green color with greenish grass.

October has additional two different appearances:

  • cloudy with a characteristic rain cloud;
  • october coverage looking like a summer;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Central and Eastern Dirt Roads  - September
metas.note: The September spring is quite easy to recognize because of the cloudy coverage, greenish shrubland and vegetation which looks kinda autumnal.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Cerro Policía - Distinct Plateau
metas.note:
Cerro Policía is a village located in north-western(ish) Rio Negro. To easily tell that you are in the nearby area, look for this very distinctive plateau:

This can be recognized from a distance from the whitish spots on the plateau
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Dirty Car - Rio Negro
metas.note: The “dirty back of the car” is the most popular car meta in Argentina. This car meta is exclusive for the northwestern(ish) part of Rio Negro province
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Dr. Atilio Oscar Viglione - Rainbow
metas.note: This village has a very unique appearance because of both the rainbow to the south and a big-looking sun to the north
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Eastern Neuqeun - Neuquen Soil?
metas.note:
Generally, in the eastern Neuquén (east of the RN40) it is very common to see reddish/maroon soil.

  • Only exception is the RP5 in Rio Negro.
  • Mind that in the northern provinces such a landscape may also occur there but predominantly you can additionally see small trees mixed with such a landscape.
  • Mind that, the similar color of soil may also be found in the northern provinces e.g. La Rioja, Salta. But in Neuquén the soil usually is accompanied by a very specific landscape, shrub-steppe landscape mixed with branchy shrubs.

In conclusion: Reddish/maroon soil + shrub-steppe landscape mixed with branchy shrubs = eastern Neuquén.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Eastern Rio Negro - Lush green landscape and light soil
metas.note:
As we can see, the eastern Rio Negro is mainly accompanied by a lush green vegetation, shrublands mixed with a grass and a light soil. Additionally, let’s pay attention to the trees. In Rio Negro province the Neuquen trees (thin and tall ones) are only seen along the Rio Negro river which connects Viedma and Neuquen cities.

The area where you can see the eastern Rio Negro landscape is marked in green whereas the Rio Negro river - as a red line.

It is worth adding that the northern Rio Negro (north of the river) does have a similar appearance to the eastern Rio Negro landscape but the northern part is less lush than the generic eastern part.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: El Maitén - Mountain Range
metas.note: El Maitén is a town located in north-western Chubut province. To easily tell that you are in this town area or nearby, look for this very distinctive mountain range to the east:
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Gobernador Gregores - North hills
metas.note: Gobernador Gregores is a town located in the central Santa Cruz province. The area near this town is very green with lots of trees and wetlands. To easily tell that you are in this town area, look for these distinctive green hills to the north:
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Grass - TDF, South Santa Cruz
metas.note: The grass-steppe landscape is characterized by a grassy landscape consisting of tufts of grass and tiny shrubs. Grass-steppe landscape also is characterized by a complete lack of bushes and trees.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: High Branchy Shrubs - Central-Northern Rio Negro
metas.note: With fields of these high branchy shrubs it is more likely that you are in the part of Rio Negro shown below(refer to the 2nd image):
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Monkey Puzzle - Western Neuquén
metas.note: Araucaria Araucana (also known as Monkey Puzzle Tree) is a species of evergreen coniferous tree found only in the central-western Neuquén province near the Chilean border.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Mountainous Neuquén - Dry mountains, exposed rock
metas.note: This type of landscape is typical of summer coverage. The Mountainous Neuquén Landscape is characterized by dry mountains with exposed rocks. There is also a large number of rivers, therefore, it’s very likely to see lots of poplar trees and bushes in the valleys. Additionally, in some places, the groves of small coniferous trees occur.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: No Center - RP5, RP50, RP11
metas.note: Outer solid white lines no center line (only applies in gen 3)
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Northeast Santa Cruz - Shrub-Steppe Landscape
metas.note:
Northeastern Santa Cruz shrub-steppe landscape is characterized by:

  • cloudy coverage;
  • dark brownish soil dirt roads;
  • tufts of grass and dark green shrubs;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Northern Santa cruz - Tiny shrubs + yellowish grass
metas.note: Northern Santa Cruz landscape is dry and is mainly accompanied by tiny shrubs + tufts of yellowish grass. Also, you can see hills and plateaus in the distance both to the south and to the north mostly always (this coverage can be gen 4).
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Northwest Chubut - May
metas.note:
Northwestern Chubut landscape in May (late autumn coverage) looks very unique. This landscape is characterized by:

  • rocky soil;
  • very large number of small coniferous and deciduous trees;
  • sunny autumnal and mountainous landscape (trees and bushes with red and orange leaves + snow-capped mountains);
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Península Valdés - Wide road
metas.note:
The distinctive features of Península Valdés Landscape are:

  • wide dirt roads (for the Peninsula itself);
  • tight sandy soil;
  • tiny yellowish grass;
  • green shrubs;
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Piedra Parada - Colossal Rock
metas.note: Piedra Parada is known for its very famous colossal rock which resulted from a volcanic eruption many millions years ago. The rock is a part of the national park which is characterized by a very rocky landscape.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Poplars - Neuquen/Trelew
metas.note: Poplars are thin and tall deciduous trees that are mainly associated with the Neuquén province - hence the common name. These trees may be found in many different places in Argentina so they are not province exclusive. However, if you see lots of poplars that are single-row planted and are accompanied by a very flat landscape* then it’s very likely that you are either in the town of Trelew (eastern Chubut province), town of Sarmiento (southern Chubut province) or in cities/towns along the Río Negro river that connects Neuquen and Viedma cities.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Puerto San Julian - Hills
metas.note:
Puerto San Julian is a town located in the central-eastern Santa Cruz province. To easily tell that you are nearby, look for these two distinctive hills (refer to the 1st image)

These hills may be visible when you are in the area marked in green, black dots are where approximately where the hillls are (refer to the 2nd image).
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Red Baron - Red hue
metas.note: Imperata Cylindrica “Red Baron” is a grass species that has a very distinctive red hue. This grass may be found throughout the Patagonia region but only in the west (western Rio Negro, western Chubut etc.). Sometimes Imperata Cylindrica may occur in very dense assemblages as shown on the first and on the second image. However, there are not many places with dense assemblages of this grass - these may be found only in the western Chubut plus southern and central Santa Cruz provinces.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

metas.name: Rio Negro shrubland - Río Negro, south La Pampa
metas.note: This type of landscape is typical of summer coverage. The Río Negro Shrubland is characterized by green shrubs and bushes, tiny/long yellowish and greenish grass plus light soil. However, the most important aspect of this landscape is the fact that there is an almost complete lack of trees. Trees may only be found near the Río Negro river.
metas.footer: From: The Comprehensive Argentina Guide by tmcdermid

In this section of the rp-6, light green cushion-looking plants (also known as Azorella Prolifera) can be seen accompanied by a shrub-steppe landscape.

NOTE: These plants can be seen elsewhere in Patagonia, so use the other characteristics to tell them apart, in this case, the shrub-steppe landscape + it's pretty flat (can be hilly in some parts but never mountainous)

metas.note:
Generally, RP63 shares a very specific landscape so the road should be very easy to recognize. The landscape is characterized by:

  • lush and green vegetation (shrub-steppes, bushes and trees);
  • rolling high and very rocky mountains;
  • diverse rock formations on the mountainsides;
